title: What is of God edifies both the preacher and the hearer
setting: This revelation came at Kirtland, Ohio, on 9 May 1831. Ohio branches had seen fainting, contortions, and claimed visions in their meetings. A local newspaper reported young converts rolling on floors. Joseph Smith had worked to curb these displays since February, but the problems went on. Elders who could not tell true spirits from false asked him for guidance.
summary: The revelation warns the elders that false spirits are deceiving the world. It says there are hypocrites in the Church who will be detected. Then the Lord invites the elders to reason together, face to face. He asks what they were ordained to do, and answers: preach by the Spirit. Teaching and receiving by the Spirit of truth edifies both sides. What does not edify is darkness, and what is of God is light. For a spirit they cannot understand, they are to ask the Father in Jesus’s name. It sends Joseph Wakefield, Parley P. Pratt, and John Corrill to strengthen the churches, and calls Edward Partridge to repent.

contextNote.title: Edification as the test
contextNote.text: The elders had accepted spirits they could not understand as coming from God. Verses 17–20 ask two questions: how is truth preached, and how is it received? The answer to both is “by the Spirit of truth”. Verse 22 gives the result: preacher and hearer understand each other and rejoice together. Verse 23 turns that result into a test: what does not edify is not of God. Verse 24 adds that light received leads to more light. In this passage, to edify means to build an understanding that both sides share.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 49–50, “That Which Is of God Is Light,” draws on verse 24 about growing light. Using verses 21–23, how could you tell whether a lesson or talk was taught and received by the Spirit?

newPeople.name: Joseph Wakefield
newPeople.why: named in 50:37 and 52:35; elder sent to strengthen the churches and later to the eastern lands

reviewNote: Read all 46 verses. Official heading gives Kirtland, May 1831, to the elders, after Joseph’s inquiry about spirits. JSP gives 9 May 1831 and documents the Ohio manifestations, including the Painesville Telegraph report of February 1831. The WebFetch summary returned the Revelation Book 1 heading (“52nd Commandment May 9th. 1831”); the page title is given here in the standard JSP form and should be confirmed.
